thread:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's KMS rekey we started seeing SCIM group deprovisions fail for ~20% of Azure/Okta syncs. Users remain in 'contractor' role after they should've been removed. Not a full outage but customer-facing.

sanjay: Ugh. Any KMS-decrypt errors in the auth logs?

maria: Paste of a truncated log from provisioning-worker: `ERROR scim_sync: decrypt failed: InvalidCiphertextException: decryption failed for envelope key alias arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:alias/redwood-rekey-2024`

ian: That looks like envelope key mismatch. Did the rekey change the key id but not update stored key version in the SCIM payload?

alex: Quick question — were there any RBAC mapping changes at the same time? I've seen sticky-role issues when mapping rules change and deprov jobs skip users due to role mismatch.

maria: We rolled KMS new alias at 03:15 UTC and a tiny RBAC tweak to treat `contractor` as non-internal (to test audit path) at 03:40. I didn't think they'd interact but timeline matches.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-4835 — "SCIM deprovision failures after KMS rekey". Pager will notify infra on escalate threshold.

eva: Can someone grep audit logs for `scim:deprovision` + `kms:decrypt` failures around 03:2* ? If decrypt is failing we might fallback to previous key alias temporarily to unblock customers.

sanjay: Running quick query now. If the provisioning service persisted encrypted envelope keys (versioned) and the code expects a specific key version, rotation could break unless we support alias resolution + rewrap. Do we have a rewrap job?

ian: We do, but it runs as a background migration and was scheduled at 04:00. Looks like some jobs hit before migration ran. Migration expects the old key to still be able to decrypt (KMS decrypt with previous key) — if old key was disabled/retired it will fail.

alex: So mitigation path: 1) Temporarily re-enable previous key/alias for 4 hours OR 2) re-run deprovision jobs only after restoring decryption path. Which is less risky?

maria: Ops + infra prefer re-enabling previous key alias briefly. But we also need to check RBAC mapping edge-case — if mapping change caused the deprov job to early-exit (role no longer flagged for deprovision), we could get users left behind even after decrypt fixed.

eva: I'll check mapping rules in prod config repo. If there's a gating check like `if role in keep_list: skip`, and contractor got flipped, that'll explain the sticky state.

sanjay: Also note audit log entries show `scim:deprovision request_id=abc123 status=errored reason=kms_decrypt` for 23 distinct requests, and separate `scim:deprovision request_id=def456 status=skipped reason=rbac_filter` for 12 requests. Two orthogonal root causes.

ian: Good catch — we have to address both. Short term: re-enable old key -> re-run failed deprov jobs for the `errored` set -> temporary rollback RBAC tweak to avoid `skipped` -> run reprov for skipped ones.

alex: Who can do the key re-enable? Need infra permissions. Tagging infra on-call in incident. @ops-team please advise.

ops-bot: @ops-team paged.

maria: I've started a list of affected customers and outbound comms draft. We should be transparent about "temporary key re-enable during remediation" and highlight we're not exposing plaintext.

eva: On audit: make sure we capture `kms_key_alias_before` and `kms_key_alias_after` in the SCIM audit entries going forward. That'll make post-rotate debugging way easier. I'll file an RFC for minimal audit schema change.

sanjay: Also let's add a pre-rotate health check in the rotation playbook: run a dry-decrypt on a small sample of envelope keys and run a sample SCIM deprov in staging under the new alias. If it fails, abort rotation.

ian: After we remediate, run a vuln triage: does storing versioned envelope keys + rotation pattern open any replay or key confusion vulnerabilities? We should document threat model.

maria: Agreed. For now, infra re-enabled the old alias, deprovisions are re-queued, and a small batch has cleared for two affected customers. Continuing to monitor. I'll post another update in ~30m.

alex: Thanks — keep on the incident thread. If anyone finds a customer data exposure pattern, escalate immediately.

maria: Quick note — sample repro command for infra if they need to reproduce locally:
```
# repro: attempt to decrypt envelope using alias
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://encrypted-envelope.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:alias/redwood-rekey-2024
```

maria: End of thread for now — monitoring + audit RFC in progress.
